title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography featuring Dutch public figures was created and distributed on a platform without the subjects' consent or knowledge. The system that generated these videos deployed face-swapping technology to create non-consensual intimate imagery, a use case it should never have enabled. The platform itself lacked content moderation sufficient to prevent upload and distribution of this material, and instead structured incentives to encourage creators to remain anonymous and maximize views. Catching this would have required either technical detection of deepfake videos before upload or human review of flagged content.

What is not established: whether the platform knowingly hosted the material or how long it remained before removal.

The incident illustrates two failures in sequence: the creation tool itself was used for a harmful purpose it could have been constrained against, and the hosting platform failed as a gatekeep. A venue that does not moderate for non-consensual intimate imagery before distribution allows harm at scale. This case prompted legal complaints from multiple victims and a parliamentary motion calling for a designated authority to take such material offline.

summary:
Multiple Dutch female celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos posted on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature numerous Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives confirmed that several victims have already filed reports or are exploring legal options.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's face is digitally placed onto an adult film actor, is classified as revenge pornography and is illegal. Users who upload material to the platform are advised to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and are paid based on views. Lawyers recommend victims file formal complaints, which allows prosecutors to attempt shutting down the website. Other options include launching a mass lawsuit, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued the person who created deepfake videos of her, resulting in a 39-year-old man receiving a suspended sentence of 180 hours of community service.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
